rounds.text: Shoppers Stop Ltd demonstrates underlying fundamental momentum with a 5-year compounded sales growth rate of 24% [E15], alongside a 5-year compounded profit growth of 14% [E18] that historically outpaced its 5-year share price growth of 6% [E21], signalling a fundamentals-led disconnect [E51]. The rules-based screen registers a score of 71 out of 100 with a BUY rating [E57], supported by positive operational catalysts including a 9% YoY sales growth [E58], a 115% YoY net profit expansion [E59], and quarterly profit growth [E61]. Capital allocation and efficiency are underscored by robust cash generation, with operating cash flow reaching Rs 838 Cr and free cash flow hitting Rs 703 Cr in Mar 2026 [E33, E34], while EV/EBITDA trades attractively at 8.68x against a sector benchmark of 11.7x [E11]. Institutional support is actively building, evidenced by domestic institutions increasing their stake to 25.82% from 21.97% [E41], and overall institutional money flow reading positive [E42]. Conceded: the business faces clear headwinds including a rich valuation with a P/E of 906x and P/B of 14.18x [E1, E2], a low return on equity of -6.4% [E13], and heavy debt-to-equity leverage of 12.26x [E35].

Shoppers Stop exhibits extreme valuation risk, trading at a P/E of 906x and a P/B of 14.18x, both of which significantly exceed sector benchmarks [E1, E2, E6, E7]. This aggressive pricing is difficult to justify given the company’s poor profitability, evidenced by a negative ROE of -6.4% and a median ROE of -6% over the last year [E13, E27]. The balance sheet is under significant pressure, with a debt-to-equity ratio of 12.26x and a current ratio of 0.85x, indicating that current liabilities exceed current assets [E35, E36]. Furthermore, compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months has collapsed by 73%, and the quarterly operating-margin trend has been decreasing for four consecutive quarters [E19, E31]. Conceded: the company generated Rs 838 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 703 Cr in free cash flow in March 2026 [E33, E34]. Despite these cash flows, the stock has suffered a 31% decline over the last year, reflecting a lack of investor confidence in the underlying fundamentals [E23, E47].

Conceded: trading at a P/E of 906x and a P/B of 14.18x [E1, E2]. However, the EV/EBITDA of 8.68x sits favorably below the sector benchmark of 11.7x, proving that enterprise valuation offers a more grounded picture than simple earnings multiples [E11]. Conceded: the TTM profit growth dropped 73% and ROE is negative [E13, E19]. Despite this, the company exhibits robust cash-generative power, printing ₹ 838 Cr in operating cash flow and ₹ 703 Cr in free cash flow in March 2026 [E33, E34]. Furthermore, the rules-based screen awards a BUY score of 71 out of 100, driven by tangible momentum including a 9% YoY sales increase and a 115% YoY net profit surge [E57, E58, E59]. Institutional backing remains solid as domestic institutions increased their stake to 25.82% while overall institutional money flow registers as positive [E41, E42].

Conceded: EV/EBITDA is 8.68x against a sector benchmark of 11.7x [E11]. However, relying on enterprise multiples ignores the staggering P/E of 906x and a P/B of 14.18x that signal an unsupported, rich valuation [E1, E2, E63]. While operating cash flow reached ₹ 838 Cr and free cash flow hit ₹ 703 Cr in March 2026 [E33, E34], this cash generation coexists with severe balance sheet vulnerability, notably a debt-to-equity ratio of 12.26x where borrowings stand at ₹ 3,457 Cr [E35, E37]. Conceded: domestic institutions raised their stake to 25.82% and institutional money flow reads positive [E41, E42]. Nevertheless, foreign institutional investors have cut their holdings from 6.85% to 1.90% [E40], and the short-term momentum cannot mask a compressed ROE of -6.4% alongside a 73% collapse in trailing twelve-month profit growth [E13, E19].
